questions.question_text:
Which labelled point is at $(3,-4)$?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.65]
\draw[gray!30,very thin](-5,-5)grid(5,5);\draw[<->](-5.5,0)--(5.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[<->](0,-5.5)--(0,5.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(3,-4)circle(2.5pt)node[below right]{$W$};\fill(-3,4)circle(2.5pt)node[above left]{$X$};\fill(-4,3)circle(2.5pt)node[above left]{$Y$};\fill(4,-3)circle(2.5pt)node[below right]{$Z$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Changed both coordinate signs when locating the point.
Swapped the coordinates and changed both signs.
Swapped the horizontal and vertical distances.

questions.solution_text:
Move $3$ units right and $4$ units down.
The labelled point is $W$.

questions.question_text:
Point $B$ lies on the $x$-axis as shown. What are its coordinates?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.7]
\draw[gray!30,very thin](-4,-3)grid(4,3);\draw[<->](-4.5,0)--(4.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[<->](0,-3.5)--(0,3.5)node[above]{$y$};\foreach \n in {-4,...,-1,1,...,4}{\node[below,font=\scriptsize]at(\n,0){$\n$};}\fill(2,0)circle(2.5pt)node[above]{$B$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Wrote the ordered pair back to front, putting the axis reading of $2$ in the vertical slot.
Counted $2$ to the right of the origin but recorded it as negative.
Wrote the pair back to front and also recorded the rightward count of $2$ as negative.

questions.solution_text:
The horizontal coordinate is $2$ and a point on the $x$-axis has $y=0$.
$B=(2,0)$

questions.question_text:
Which pair gives the coordinates of $C$ and $D$ in that order?
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large},scale=0.65]
\draw[gray!30,very thin](-5,-5)grid(5,5);\draw[<->](-5.5,0)--(5.5,0)node[right]{$x$};\draw[<->](0,-5.5)--(0,5.5)node[above]{$y$};\fill(-1,4)circle(2.5pt)node[above left]{$C$};\fill(4,-2)circle(2.5pt)node[below right]{$D$};\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

options.why: Wrote each point vertical-coordinate first, swapping the two entries of every pair.
Read the correct grid distances but dropped the negative sign on every count made left or down.
Swapped the two entries of every pair and also dropped the negative sign on every left or down count.

questions.solution_text:
$C$ is $1$ left and $4$ up: $C=(-1,4)$.
$D$ is $4$ right and $2$ down: $D=(4,-2)$.
